title: [trd:trd-2026-48f7b420-foreman-beads-task-provider:pr:1a] PR 1: Foundation (TaskProvider behaviour + BrRunner boundary + ProviderError + JsonSchemaCache + ConcurrencyLimiter + 3 surgical config updates)
description: PR 1 of TRD: TRD: Foreman × Beads Rust — Task-Provider Integration. Contains 22 tasks. Shippable state: Operators can register providers via `Application.put_env(:foreman_server, :task_provider, providers: [...])`. The `ForemanServer.TaskProvider` behaviour declares 11 callbacks (`name/0`, `capabilities/0`, `available?/0`, `list_ready/2`, `get/2`, `claim/3`, `complete/3`, `fail/3`, `reopen/3`, `set_priority/3`, `add_dependency/3`). The `ForemanServer.TaskProviders.BrRunner` behaviour defines `cmd/3` (arity 3) — the contract implemented by `SystemBrRunner` (sole `System.cmd("br", ...)` site) and `BrRunnerMock` (compile-time bound via `Application.compile_env`). The `ForemanServer.TaskProviders.JsonSchemaCache` GenServer fetches and caches `br schema` JSON outputs at boot, exposes `validate(:ready_issue, payload)` and `validate(:issue_details, payload)`, refreshes every 24h, and emits `[:foreman_server, :task_provider, :beads, :capabilities, :refreshed]` on contract-version change (REQ-002-3). The `ForemanServer.TaskProviders.ConcurrencyLimiter` GenServer enforces `max_in_flight: 4` + per-call `timeout_ms: 30_000` and emits `BR_TIMEOUT_QUEUE` envelopes on queue timeout. The `ForemanServer.TaskProviders.ProviderError` typed struct carries 7 allowlisted context keys. The `ForemanServer.TaskProviders.BeadsAdapter.CodeMap` data-only 12-row mapping mediates between `br.code` envelopes and Foreman closed-vocab codes via `CodeMap.ProviderErrorInput` (a two-layer API: Layer 1 `ProviderErrorInput` struct + `from_br_envelope/1`/`from_local/5` constructors; Layer 2 `translate/3`/`translate_unknown/3`/`build_provider_error/3` all share `(input, command, stderr_byte_count) :: %ProviderError{}`). v1 has no `SensitiveFieldScrubber` — REQ-019 redaction is emission-only: argv passed to `br` is unscrubbed (original). `scrub_argv/1` (defined in PR 1b's TRD-023) produces a verbatim-copy with sentinels replaced for telemetry/log/ProviderError.context only. PR 1a is foundation only — the 8 operational callback impls + per-project registry state + post-execution lifecycle wire-up land in PR 1b.
close_reason: PR-1a Foundation: 22 tasks closed. TaskProvider behaviour (11 callbacks), BrRunner boundary (SystemBrRunner sole System.cmd site replaced via Port.open), ProviderError (7 allowlisted context keys), JsonSchemaCache (24h TTL + capabilities refresh), ConcurrencyLimiter (4 in-flight + 30s timeout), 3 surgical config updates (boot child, providers config, telemetry). ## Task: TRD-001
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-6af02293-otp-agent-runtime.md#trd-001
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-6af02293-otp-agent-runtime.md#req-001

--- TRD Context ---
### Selected: Option B — Fully Supervised Execution Subsystem

Implement a dedicated `ForemanServer.AgentRuntime.Supervisor` with separate registry, adapter catalog, and invocation supervision responsibilities. Routing and failure-policy resolution remain pure modules. Each call to `AgentRuntime.execute/3` creates a short-lived supervised invocation process that owns selection, timeout, retries, fallback history, telemetry, and adapter execution.

This option was selected because adapter crashes and hung local processes are explicit PRD risks. Separating durable runtime catalog state from short-lived execution state makes failure containment observable and testable without turning the public facade into a stateful bottleneck.

### Alternatives Considered

#### Option A — Minimal Extension

Implement registry, routing, fallback, and adapter invocation primarily in one `AgentRuntime` GenServer with one task supervisor.

- **Pros:** fewest modules; fastest initial delivery; simple startup.
- **Cons:** serial catalog calls and orchestration share one mailbox; policy, ranking, retry, and execution lifecycle become coupled; one defect has a wider blast radius.
- **Complexity impact:** low initial complexity, high extension complexity.
- **Risk profile:** medium-high operational coupling; rejected because a hung or overloaded orchestration process can impair unrelated calls.

#### Option B — Fully Supervised Execution Subsystem (selected)

Use a facade, adapter catalog, invocation registry, dynamic invocation supervisor, pure router, policy behaviour, failure-policy resolver, and adapter modules.

- **Pros:** explicit interfaces; concurrent calls are isolated; deterministic routing is independently testable; invocation crashes do not corrupt adapter registration state.
- **Cons:** more modules and supervision tests; careful ownership is required for timeout and Port termination.
- **Complexity impact:** highest upfront component count, controlled long-term complexity.
- **Risk profile:** low runtime blast radius, medium implementation risk around process lifecycle.

#### Option C — Layered Runtime

Use a stateless facade over a small runtime catalog with `Task.Supervisor` for calls, while keeping routing and fallback in the facade call path.

- **Pros:** balanced module count; leverages standard tasks; simpler than a dedicated invocation process.
- **Cons:** cancellation and fallback history ownership are less explicit; task exits require careful normalization; future streaming would force lifecycle redesign.
- **Complexity impact:** medium.
- **Risk profile:** medium; viable, but less explicit than Option B for timeout and crash recovery.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
Correction to the prior commit 6ceba8a3.

The commit message and earlier comment overstated what
`BackendAdapter.@type capabilities :: Capabilities.input()`
provides. Specifically:

> "an adapter whose `capabilities/0` returns a map missing a
> required key will fail to compile against `@behaviour BackendAdapter`"

This is false. `@behaviour` only checks callback name and arity at
compile time; Elixir's compiler does not validate the shape of a
callback's return value. `Capabilities.input()` is a type alias used
for documentation and Dialyzer; it is **not** enforced by `mix compile`.

What the alias does provide:

- A named, documented contract for the callback's expected shape
  (the four required keys and the two optional keys, with permissive
  inner types so the validator can still report field-specific errors).
- A single source of truth shared by `BackendAdapter.@callback
  capabilities/0`, `BackendAdapter.validate_capabilities/1`, and
  `Capabilities.validate/1`.
- A target for future Dialyzer coverage once the repo opts into it
  (no PLT, no `dialyzer` mix task, and no `mix.exs` entry today).

What it does **not** provide:

- Compile-time rejection of malformed capability maps.
- Any runtime effect.

The runtime safety net remains `Capabilities.validate/1` (called by
`BackendAdapter.validate_capabilities/1` and `AgentRuntime.register/1`),
which returns a field-specific error and never stores an invalid map.

No code change required. This is a documentation correction only.
